name: Demonology / Diabolist
note: Soul Shards are one of the seven NEVER-SECRET power types, so the largest decision in the spec — do I have five shards for Tyrant — is an exact Lua comparison rather than a curve. Base spell ids only: Bind unions base/override/tooltip/live into the row, so neither transform needs a hardcoded override id.

abilities.note: Aura dependencies only: these are not enhanced CDM entries and never enter Signal. They exist so a sealed display can name a subject — the count or the clock the CLIENT reads. cap never learns any of their values.
Doom is a DEBUFF cap puts on the target, which is why it carries a unit. Its refresh window is the client's own arithmetic, per spell (V19).

The armed Art that transforms row 9 into Infernal Bolt. The id is TIER-3-SOURCED and a wrong aura id dies SILENT — the slot matches nothing forever, indistinguishable from a refusal (the cast-id/aura-id trap, KB 3.5.2). Flight question; @verify-ingame on the id.

talents_note: Node + entry from knowledge/classes/warlock/demonology/talents.json @ 12.1. This is what talent.to_hell_and_back and talent.doom in the APL mean, read as themselves rather than through a proxy (Talents.lua explains why IsSpellKnown and charge counts are both refused). `spell` is documentation only — nothing resolves through it.

entries.note: Its rung gate is buff.demonic_core.stack<=1, which is a SEALED count — so the row carries no readable cue at all and the display does the whole of the work. Below two Cores the band draws nothing and the row is an ordinary candidate; at two it hatches and marks itself, which is the row RULED OUT by a fact cap never read.

states.note: The row rules ITSELF out on a fact cap never read — hatch plus a negative mark, both named by the band so both clear together. This closed the catalog's second defeat (DEM-14).

entries.note: A CHOICE NODE **and** the base of a transform — two independent facts, both true. The choice: both ids have their own Essential row and exactly one exists on a build, so the second goes in `alt` rather than through R7. The transform: whichever one exists becomes a dispel while its OWN cooldown runs — Imp Lord `1276452` → Singe Magic `132411` via override row `1276623`, Fel Ravager `1276467` → Devour Magic `388215` via `1276610`, both `EffectAura` 333, misc-form. So this row is never swiped by the Grimoire's 120 s: any swipe on it is the dispel's own 15 s. Cue K is what rules the row out instead.

markers.note: Cue K, and it reads this row's OWN identity — `ha_banks_bulwark` and `star_counter` are the shape, not cue D, which reads another row's. `overrideSpellID ~= spellID` here means the Grimoire's cooldown is running and the button on the icon is the dispel it becomes. cap's overlay reads the ROTATION; while the row is the dispel it is not the rotation entry the reader is looking for, so `blocked` says *this is not your Grimoire* — a statement about identity, never advice to avoid a castable button.

V21, and it is the fact cue K leaves out — so it says it in cue K's own badge rather than beside it. Cue K rules this row out on identity; it says nothing about WHEN the row stops being the dispel, which is what a ramp is waiting for. Since 2026-08-28 the two are one statement: this marker declares `blocked`, and a `blocked` badge whose block is a cooldown draws that cooldown live — a red radial on the real remaining with a white countdown in it — instead of `timer_CW_50`, a picture of a clock face frozen at 50 % on a row where the real remaining exists and is reachable. `baseoncd` is the readable half — `C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown(baseID).isActive`, NeverSecret and plain in restricted combat — and it gates a badge whose arc and numeral the CLIENT draws off the base spell's own duration object, which cap hands over and never reads. ⚠ The dial reads the BOUND ROW's base id, not this declaration's `spell`: the entry covers both halves of a choice node through `alt`, so on a Fel Ravager build the declared id is the wrong half. The `ability` here names the subject, not the spell that is read.

markers.display_exception: AUTHORED PAST THE APL, in the same style as cue I. `actions.diabolist+=/grimoire_imp_lord` (simc-apl.md rung 3) is unconditional — upstream presses the Grimoire the moment it is up and never asks about Tyrant. The evidence that players do otherwise is 200 Season-2 M+ parses (zone 55, top-25 DPS per dungeon, 82 players, 2467 Grimoire casts): within-pull Grimoire gap median 125.2 s on a 120 s cooldown, landing a median 4.4 s BEFORE Tyrant, |delta| <= 10 s in 70.7 % of pairs. A synthetic strictly-on-cooldown control run against the same logs lands at chance (31.8 % against a 33.3 % uniform baseline), so the alignment is not an artefact of two 120 s cooldowns drifting together. Banking a Grimoire a whole Tyrant cycle: 0.9 %. Players NUDGE, they do not HOLD — which is why the band is narrow and one-sided-in-effect rather than a hold until Tyrant. ⚠ Its weaknesses, recorded beside it: the control is SYNTHETIC rather than a second population; the observations are not independent (82 players, one of whom holds 5 of 8 rank-1 slots); top-parse selection; ten days of data. ⚠ `3` and `10` are NOT measured optima — `3` is 2 x gcd.max, the floor at which a press still lands before Tyrant, and `10` is rung 6's own idiom (`12 - gcd.max` = 10.5, `20 + gcd.max` = 21.5) narrowed to one cast rather than two.
markers.note: The band that makes the Grimoire's own hold legible, and the second display on this row to draw as a live dial. While the Grimoire is READY and Tyrant's cooldown is inside (3, 10), the client paints `blocked` and the badge is Tyrant's remaining — the thing the reader is actually waiting on. ⚠ The `!baseoncd` term is load-bearing and not decoration: this row is never swiped (the button on it is the dispel, with its own 15 s), so without it the band would arm while the Grimoire itself is on cooldown and two dials would claim the same badge. `baseoncd` is the one readable term that says which of the two is the live question.

states.condition: displaying the dispel, and the DISPEL's own 15 s cooldown is running
states.exception: No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press. The swipe here is Blizzard's and it rules the row out before cap has an opinion, but it belongs to the DISPEL: `RecoveryTime = 15000` on Singe Magic / Devour Magic, against the Grimoires' `CategoryRecoveryTime = 120000` [T1 db2: SpellCooldowns @ 12.1.0.69214]. The swipe on this row is the 15 s one; the Grimoire's 120 s is V21's badge, on the corner, and the two clocks are both on screen and mean different things.
states.note: The state that keeps `cd` honest on this row. `grimoire_shows_dispel` and `grimoire_base_cooldown` are both still true here — the identity has not changed and the Grimoire's own clock is running — but the swipe eliminates first and cap draws no cue over a row Blizzard has already ruled out. What remains is the dial itself, carrying no verdict: it says when the row stops being the dispel, on a row that is dark for a different reason.

states.condition: displaying the dispel, the dispel off cooldown, and the ramp hold does not apply
states.exception: No rung expresses it. The priority list presses the Grimoire and says nothing about the utility spell the button becomes underneath — and Blizzard does not rule the row out here either, because the button on the icon is a different spell with its own cooldown, which is not running.
states.note: Cue K, drawn AS V21. One badge, not two: the `blocked` verdict and the Grimoire's own remaining are the same statement, so the red radial with the countdown in it IS the cue and the still clock glyph is not drawn over it. `grimoire_shows_dispel` and `grimoire_base_cooldown` both declare `blocked` here and agree by construction — the row is the dispel exactly while the Grimoire's cooldown runs.

states.condition: displaying the dispel, the dispel off cooldown, and the ramp open — Tyrant READY below five shards
states.exception: Neither half is a rung: cue K is an identity statement the priority list has no vocabulary for, and the ramp hold is authored past rungs 3 and 4, which are unconditional.
states.note: The co-occurrence, stated. `grimoire_awaits_shards` carries no identity term, so it arms on the transformed row too and the icon wears BOTH cards — same hue, both negative, so the row reads as held either way. `blocked` is the one that governs — it outranks cue I in the badge stack — and here it governs as the live dial: the ramp's card is still literally true, the board IS below five shards, but it is advice about a button that is not on the icon, and what the reader needs is when the button comes back. DEM-4, DEM-10 and DEM-12.

states.condition: ready and displaying the Grimoire, Reign of Tyranny talented, Tyrant's cooldown inside (3, 10)
states.exception: Authored PAST the priority list, in cue I's own style: rung 3 is unconditional, so no rung expresses a hold for Tyrant. The evidence that players hold anyway is on the marker (`grimoire_awaits_tyrant`, `display_exception`) — 2467 Grimoire casts across 200 Season-2 M+ parses, landing a median 4.4 s before Tyrant against a synthetic on-cooldown control at chance.
states.note: The band, and the second thing on this row to draw as a live dial — this time it is TYRANT'S clock, not the Grimoire's, because Tyrant is what the hold is waiting for. The client evaluates the two-sided band and paints the badge; cap never learns Tyrant's remaining and hands the same duration object to the arc and to the numeral. UNFLOWN.

states.condition: ready and displaying the Grimoire, Tyrant READY, below five shards
states.exception: Authored PAST the priority list. Rungs 3 and 4 are unconditional — upstream presses the Grimoire on cooldown — so no rung expresses this hold. It is the summon block's shared ramp opinion, uniform across four rows and playtest-gated.
states.note: Cue I. Authored PAST the APL — the rung is unconditional — and playtest-gated.

excludes.why: The same readable term, both ways round: `grimoire_base_cooldown` arms on `baseoncd(grimoire)` and `grimoire_awaits_tyrant` on `!baseoncd(grimoire)`. Written as an explicit negation rather than left to the band, because this row is never swiped — the button on it is the dispel, with its own 15 s — so nothing else would have kept the Tyrant band off a Grimoire that is itself on cooldown, and two dials would have claimed one badge.

Cue K arms on `identity(grimoire, "transformed")`, and the row is transformed exactly while the Grimoire's own cooldown runs (the entry note: override row `1276623` / `1276610`, `EffectAura` 333). `grimoire_awaits_tyrant` carries `!baseoncd(grimoire)`, which is that same fact negated, so the two cannot be true together.

Cue I requires Tyrant READY — cooldown remaining zero — and the Tyrant band only draws while that remaining is inside (3, 10). A ready Tyrant is outside the band by construction, the same exclusion `call_dreadstalkers` states for its own band.

entries.note: The single biggest decision in the spec, and it is READABLE: rung 8 is soul_shard=5, read as a hold. Gated on readiness because a hold badge on a greyed icon says nothing.

entries.note: Two halves of one rung, split exactly on the readable/sealed line: active_enemies>2|talent.to_hell_and_back is readable and is the cue; wild_imps.stack>=6 is sealed and is the display. The display is V17's COMPLEMENT — it draws BELOW the threshold and clears at it — and it is the first time a sealed fact enters elimination rather than merely being displayed.

markers.note: THE ONE STATE THE BAND CANNOT REACH, and it needs cap's own readable latch. With no Wild Imp at all there is no aura, so the client hides the whole button and every sink on it draws nothing. The `aura` predicate is readable and an unbound row reads UNKNOWN rather than false, so this stays dark rather than asserting the imps are gone. ⚠ THE `0` IS CAP'S OWN LITERAL (V22), and this marker's own `when` is what licenses it: `!aura(wild_imp)` MEANS zero, so the numeral asserts nothing cap did not already establish readably. Everywhere else on this row the count is the client's, out of an AuraContainer FontString cap never reads back — which is exactly why the zero could not come from there, and why it was drawn as a frozen clock glyph until 2026-08-28. The row is one grammar now: 0 → red 1-5 → gold 6+.

Rung 9's readable half GATES its sealed half, and that is the whole of this pair. The band's upper polarity is cap's positive ink — `count.rgb` is byte-identical to the `priority` and `capped` cue hues — so under V5.1 a gold numeral is cap saying `press this`. Ungated it said so in single target with To Hell and Back untalented, where rung 9 cannot fire at all and `implosion_st_only` is simultaneously ruling the row out: cap's own promotion ink on a button the priority list has closed. `when` is AND-only, so the disjunction `active_enemies>2|talent.to_hell_and_back` is two markers; the gates are written MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE rather than as a plain OR because each corner display claims its own stack slot by declaration, so two live at once would draw two numerals at two corners. This is the AoE-toggle half. The NUMERAL, not the mark: `how many more` is exactly the live question below six, and the hatch beside it already carries `ruled out`. At six the count RECOLORS instead of clearing — same numeral, opposite polarity, no hatch, because a positive band may not wear one.

Rung 9's readable half GATES its sealed half, and that is the whole of this pair. The band's upper polarity is cap's positive ink — `count.rgb` is byte-identical to the `priority` and `capped` cue hues — so under V5.1 a gold numeral is cap saying `press this`. Ungated it said so in single target with To Hell and Back untalented, where rung 9 cannot fire at all and `implosion_st_only` is simultaneously ruling the row out: cap's own promotion ink on a button the priority list has closed. `when` is AND-only, so the disjunction `active_enemies>2|talent.to_hell_and_back` is two markers; the gates are written MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE rather than as a plain OR because each corner display claims its own stack slot by declaration, so two live at once would draw two numerals at two corners. This is the To Hell and Back half: the talent makes Implosion a single-target press, so the count is live with the AoE toggle OFF. `!aoe` is what keeps it disjoint from `implosion_imps_aoe`. A refused `talent` read is UNKNOWN, and a gate reads a blind term as withheld (`Signal.Evaluate`), so this fails dark rather than painting on a build cap could not resolve.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, no Wild Imp out at all
states.note: Cue H, and it draws a red `0` (V22) rather than the shared clock glyph — cap's own literal, licensed by this state's own readable term. ⚠ No aura means no sealed sink draws either — the band CANNOT reach this state, which is exactly why the readable latch exists, and why the zero cannot come from the band the way 1-5 and 6+ do. With the AoE toggle on, or To Hell and Back talented, a band marker IS gated on here and still draws nothing: the client shows no button for an aura that is absent (`excludes`).

states.condition: ready, AoE mode OFF, To Hell and Back not talented, imps out
states.note: Cue G alone, and it is the WHOLE row at every imp count. The band is gated off here — rung 9's readable half is false, so neither `implosion_imps_aoe` nor `implosion_imps_thab` is licensed to paint — which is what collapses this state back into one appearance. ⚠ Until 2026-08-26 the band drew here regardless, so at six or more imps the row wore the red `aoe_only` badge (right: the rung cannot fire) beside a GOLD numeral in cap's own promotion ink (wrong: nothing is loaded on a button the priority list has closed). Silence is the trade: cap no longer says how many imps are out in single target, and it no longer says the wrong thing.

states.condition: ready, AoE on (or To Hell and Back talented), 1-5 Wild Imps
states.note: Hatch, plate and the RED numeral out of one FontString, from whichever of the two gated markers this build licenses — `implosion_imps_aoe` under the toggle, `implosion_imps_thab` on a To Hell and Back build. The band is the ONLY eliminator, so the verdict names it: the client evaluated cap's rule against a secret.

states.condition: ready, AoE on (or To Hell and Back talented), 6 or more Wild Imps
states.note: The numeral recolors GOLD and the hatch clears: banked, the press is loaded. No hatch — a positive band may not wear one. The gold is only reachable through a gate that says rung 9 can actually fire, which is the point of the pair: `implosion_imps_aoe` under the toggle, `implosion_imps_thab` on a To Hell and Back build.

overlaps.why: Single target without To Hell and Back, and no imps out either — both fire, and the corner shows the red `0`. `blocked` (rank 3) occludes `aoe_only` (rank 7) in the z-stack, and the reading is unharmed: both say skip, and the one that draws says the more specific thing — there is nothing to implode. ⚠ This WAS a state (`imp_st_and_no_imps`, deleted 2026-08-28), written when badges flowed down the right edge and its note claimed *"both badges flow in `rank` order"*. The stack collapsed to one badge deep on 2026-08-27 and that stopped being true; a state card describing a badge nobody can see is not a situation the player sees. Nothing else about it is lost: no sink draws here for two independent reasons that both still hold — rung 9's readable half is false so neither band marker is gated on, and with no Wild Imp aura there would be nothing for one to paint anyway.

excludes.why: Cue G needs the AoE toggle OFF; this band is gated ON it. One predicate, both polarities — so the badge that says `wrong mode` can never stand beside the numeral that says `banked`.
Cue G needs To Hell and Back UNTALENTED; this band is gated on it being talented. One predicate, both polarities.
`aoe` and `!aoe` — disjoint by construction, and written down because two corner displays claim two stack slots: if both could draw, the row would carry the same count as two numerals on two corners.

Not a contradiction in the gates — the toggle can be on with no imps out — but the SINK has no subject: with no Wild Imp aura the client shows no button, so nothing on it draws. Cue H is the readable latch that covers exactly this, and it is the one state a sealed band structurally cannot reach.
The same absence: To Hell and Back talented with no imps out leaves the gate true and the sink subjectless, so cue H draws alone.

entries.note: Two lives, one lane: both are shard spenders. The identity carries the transform with no cue, because Ruination outranks the ordinary press by one rung and both are pressed from this position. ⚠ But the two HOLDS are rung-11 facts and both carry `identity(hand_of_guldan, "base")` to say so: rung 10 (Ruination) is unconditional, so nothing the window rule knows can hold it.

markers.note: Sense.buildReads asks affordability of the LIVE id, so this is Ruination's cost — which is none — on the transformed row and three shards on the base one. One marker, both lives, correct in each.

The catalog's only sealed band on a spender, and the mirror of the Tyrant hold: Tyrant holds ITSELF below five shards (readable); Hand of Gul'dan holds itself while Tyrant is nearly here (sealed). Gated on resource because rung 11's |soul_shard=5 makes the spend unconditional at cap, and on affordability so it never lands on a starved row. ⚠ `identity(hand_of_guldan, "base")` scopes the hold to the row's BASE life. Both holds are derived from rung 11; while Ruination is armed the row displays rung 10, which is UNCONDITIONAL and ranked above rung 11 — holding it there would withhold a press the APL makes without any condition at all.

The READABLE half of the same window rule (cue I): Tyrant READY at sub-five shards holds the spend — rung 11's remains>5 is false at zero remaining. Cue F covers `nearly here`; this covers `here, board not built`. ⚠ `identity(hand_of_guldan, "base")` scopes the hold to the row's BASE life. Both holds are derived from rung 11; while Ruination is armed the row displays rung 10, which is UNCONDITIONAL and ranked above rung 11 — holding it there would withhold a press the APL makes without any condition at all.

states.condition: the live id is unaffordable
states.note: Cue E, and it says `building` rather than `starved` since 2026-08-28. ⚠ THE CLIENT ALREADY PAINTS THIS ROW: `RefreshIconColor` tints an unaffordable icon with ITEM_NOT_ENOUGH_MANA_COLOR, which is why the state declares it. A `starved` badge spent cap's one corner restating Blizzard, where `building` says the thing the client does not — the board is still being built, keep placing — which is what the player does about it. The `when` did not move and is still correct in both lives: three shards as Hand of Gul'dan, none as Ruination.

states.condition: affordable, below five shards, Tyrant's cooldown ends within 5 s
states.note: Cue F. The client evaluates the band; cap never learns Tyrant's remaining.

states.condition: affordable, below five shards, Tyrant READY
states.note: Cue I, the readable half of the window rule. F covers `Tyrant nearly here`; this covers `Tyrant here, board not built`.

states.condition: Ruination armed — the row's TRANSFORMED life
states.note: Rung 10, and the only rung in `actions.diabolist` with NO condition on it. Both window holds carry `identity(hand_of_guldan, "base")` and therefore withhold here, so this is an ordinary open row reached with nothing on it — which is the honest drawing, because in this life there is no state in which the APL would not press it. Cue E cannot fire either: Ruination costs no shards, so `affordable` is always true. ⚠ AND IT RENDERS EXACTLY AS `hog_press` DOES — same verdict `open`, no cues, no sealed. The two states differ only in `apl` (rung 10 vs rung 11) and in their `condition` prose; the transform itself is drawn by the ICON and V13, not by anything in the state table. So a scenario row on this ability that wears no cue cannot say which of the two it is an instance of, and the walk's prose is the only thing that can. Stated here rather than fixed: the fix is the project-wide one, pinning a scenario row to a named state instead of to the cue keys it draws.

states.condition: affordable, and no hold applies
states.note: Reached by elimination. The ordinary spend, and the button that builds the imps Implosion waits for. ⚠ Renders identically to `hog_ruination` — see that state's note.

excludes.why: Cue E fires only when the live id is UNaffordable; cue F is gated on `affordable` precisely so it never lands on a starved row.
Same gate: cue I carries `affordable(hand_of_guldan)` for exactly this reason.

A READY Tyrant is outside the within-5 band BY CONSTRUCTION, and the construction is cap's own. `Channel.HoldPoints(within)` builds `{ {0,0}, {LIVE,1}, {within,0} }` on a **Step** curve (`Channel.ArmHold`), and Step holds the previous point's value — so at zero remaining the curve evaluates to 0 and the band cannot paint. Cue I carries `ready(summon_demonic_tyrant)`, which is exactly that zero. ⚠ Nothing here is sealed: the SECRET is the remaining time, the POINTS are cap's, and the shape of a curve cap authored is not something it is waiting to learn. This was a state (`hog_both_holds`) hedged with an in-game-verify marker until 2026-08-28, one row over from `call_dreadstalkers`, whose `excludes` had the same fact stated correctly the whole time.

entries.note: The pilot's row, and the pilot had the number wrong: the APL says soul_shard<4, so the overcap badge lights at FOUR and not at three.

markers.note: Demonbolt appears in actions.diabolist ONLY gated on buff.demonic_core.react, so with no Core there is no rung at all. This is also V11's hatch at zero Cores — the one state a sealed display can never decorate, because with no aura there is no button — and it needs no new vocabulary: a negative cue already hatches the row.

The first marker in any catalog that reads ANOTHER ROW'S identity. Rung 12 puts an armed Infernal Bolt above Demonbolt, and only below three shards. ⚠ It stays READABLE-ONLY, and `db_yields_window` beside it carries the clock — the Grimoire row's shape (`grimoire_shows_dispel` + `grimoire_base_cooldown`), and the reason is that a cue is the thing that HATCHES the row. A display marker never contributes a cue (`Signal.markersOf` routes it to `verdict.gates`), so folding the display into this marker would have traded cap's readable elimination for a picture: the badge would still draw, and the red skip hatch under it would not.

markers.display_exception: `art_mother_of_chaos` appears in no rung of the Demonology list, and this display may draw it anyway because IT IS THE DURATION OF THE HOLD ITSELF. Rung 12 outranks Demonbolt exactly while row 9 is displaying Infernal Bolt, and row 9 is displaying Infernal Bolt exactly while the Art is armed — so the aura's remaining IS how long this row stays held, which is the one quantity the badge was failing to say. It carries no polarity to argue about: the arc is `blocked`'s own red and it promotes nothing — the same ground `ib_art_clock`'s exception stands on, one row over, over the same aura. Declared rather than exempted by category.
markers.note: V21's THIRD SUPPLIER: cue D's badge is the armed Art's own remaining — a red radial the client drains off the aura's duration — instead of `timer_CW_50`, a picture of a clock face frozen at 50 % beside a hold whose whole content is *how long*. ⚠ ITS `when` IS CUE D's, TERM FOR TERM, and both terms are needed: the aura filter alone would paint the clock at three or more shards, where the row is not held at all. entries.note: Default membership (ready-self): a filler is always a scan candidate. The row changed KIND is said by the icon itself; the ordering correction lives on Demonbolt, which is the row that has to move. Nothing here is load-bearing for visibility — Shadow Bolt has no cooldown, so `ready` never goes false. ⚠ AND NO `alt` ON THE ABILITY, WHICH IS ALSO AUTHORED — checked in the code 2026-08-27 rather than assumed, because this entry cites BOTH the Shadow Bolt rung (`diabolist` 15) and the Infernal Bolt rung (`diabolist` 16) while the ability declares one id, 686, with no `alt`. `alt` exists for a DIFFERENT ROW, never for an override on this one — so Havoc's base-only note and Retribution's four `alt` declarations are not rival conventions but the two halves of one rule. `Bind.buildRow` sets `base = info.spellID` and puts it in `row.spellIDs` unconditionally, beside the override, the tooltip id and the live id, and `Catalog.findRow` matches ANY member; so cooldownID 34990 answers to 686 whether the row is wearing Shadow Bolt or Infernal Bolt, and the base id binds in both lives. The `alt` cases are the other shape: Templar Strike, Hammer of Wrath and this catalog's own `grimoire` choice node each carry their OWN `info.spellID`, so a declared base alone would find nothing. Infernal Bolt has no Essential row of its own in any set (Category-2 TrackedBuff, OrderIndex 58/59 — `catalog.md`'s row-set table), so an `alt` of 433891 would match nothing today and, if a TrackedBuff row for it were ever laid out, would bind the WRONG row. The same reading covers Ruination riding Hand of Gul'dan.

defeats_unreferenced.why: Target selection is a statement about a SURFACE, not about a button. The rung it quotes is Demonbolt's 13, but `target_if` is unsayable on every row cap draws — a Cooldown Manager row is a button and "press this at that enemy" has nowhere to go on one. Destruction authors the same defeat verbatim as its own item 4. Attributing it to Demonbolt would tell a reader that row is where cap gave up, when the row is right and only the target choice is unsaid.

No entry is its site. Art: Overlord changes no button, so there is no row cap would draw it on — fact-classification.md's routing column for it reads "nothing — noted because it is one measurement from closing".
